BiblicalUsage: Bathsheba is the wife of Uriah the Hittite whom David sees from his roof and takes. She is the mother of the child who dies and then of Solomon, and the queen mother who comes to David in his old age and to Solomon on his throne to plead for Adonijah's life and for her own place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Bathsheba's name carries both the sin and the grace of the story, because the same woman who was taken in adultery becomes the mother of the king who builds the temple. God does not erase her, and I hold that her place in the genealogy of Christ is proof that grace writes names the world would rather forget.
